Linda — following up with a quick interim note. Our metering export attached (redwood_token_log_sample.txt) includes the top 1200 requests by token count across the May billing window and shows a concentrated burst on 2024-05-17 between 02:10–02:24 UTC from api_key prefix "ak_live_7f3".

Observations so far:
- The burst includes a mix of long-generation calls (avg completion_tokens ~ 8.1k) and batched embedding requests.
- The api_key prefix does not match the prefixes we have on file for your primary production key (ak_live_1a2). We see an inactive legacy key that was scheduled for rotation (ak_live_7f3) that should have been deactivated on 2024-05-10; our logs show it remained active because a staging host in your environment continued to call the endpoint.
- No automatic routing fallbacks were triggered; model used was main-gen-v1.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether the rotation completed in your key management system? If that key is in your staging environment we can provide a block and retroactive attribution mapping to pull those tokens into a staging usage bucket (which would lower billed production usage).

Attaching: redwood_token_log_sample.txt (sample). Will follow with full per-request CSV in the next email.
